name: Supercam S350

placement_rationale.text: 6 km is the Supercam crew's launch/control depth, not the 100–120 km comms range its own characteristics report. Placed one notch deeper than the Orlan-10/Leleka-100 pair at 4 km, this sits just past doctrine.md §2's 1–5 km close-reconnaissance band and is still comfortably inside the wider drone-dense corridor (~30 km either side of the front) — a plausible, slightly more conservative launch posture for a system this catalog itself compares against Zala Z-16 in the same tactical-reconnaissance niche. (Nudged 6→5.6 km from this category's shared round-number value so it doesn't literally coincide with side_b-uav-zala-z-16 on the map's distance axis — a small, deterministic spread within the same band, not a new plausibility claim beyond what's already argued above.)

characteristics: Strength: Longer comms range (100-120km) than the Zala Z-16 in the same general weight class
Limitation: No stated counter-drone evasion mechanisms, unlike some competing types in the same catalog
Estimated quantity available: Fleet size not disclosed
employment_notes: Represents a separate Russian manufacturer/product line from Zala and Orlan, indicating a fragmented rather than single-standardized Russian tactical drone industrial base
contrast_vs_traditional: Supercam fills the same persistent tactical-reconnaissance niche as Zala Z-16 — cheap enough and simple enough to fly repeatedly over a sector, which is precisely the pattern doctrine.md describes letting both sides map enemy positions over 2–7 days rather than through any single high-value reconnaissance sortie.
